definitions.gloss: kudzu vine (Pueraria montana); the plant itself
definitions.explanation: A vigorous climbing vine native to East Asia. One of the {秋|あき}の{七草|ななくさ} (seven autumn flowers) in Japan; the root is harvested for food and medicine.
A fine white starch made from the root of the kudzu plant. Used in traditional Japanese sweets and to thicken sauces. Sometimes labeled in English as "kuzu".

examples.japanese: {葛|くず}の{花|はな}が{咲|さ}いている。
examples.english: The kudzu vines are in flower.

examples.japanese: {葛|くず}は{秋|あき}の{七草|ななくさ}の{一|ひと}つだ。
examples.english: Kudzu is one of the seven flowers of autumn.

examples.japanese: {裏|うら}の{山|やま}には{葛|くず}が{一面|いちめん}に{広|ひろ}がっている。
examples.english: Kudzu has spread across the entire mountain behind us.
I thickened it with kudzu starch.

examples.japanese: {本|ほん}{葛|くず}は{高級|こうきゅう}な{和菓子|わがし}に{使|つか}われる。
examples.english: Pure kudzu starch is used in high-end Japanese sweets.

examples.japanese: {葛|くず}を{水|みず}で{溶|と}いて、{熱|あつ}いだしに{加|くわ}えるとなめらかなあんになる。
examples.english: Dissolve kudzu in water and add it to hot dashi to make a smooth thickened sauce.

notes:
Do not confuse with {屑|くず} (scrap, trash, worthless person), which is a homophone written with a different kanji. The two have nothing to do with each other semantically.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {葛|くず}の{根|ね}: kudzu root
- {本|ほん}{葛|くず}: pure kudzu starch (high grade)
- {葛|くず}{粉|こ}: kudzu powder
- {葛|くず}{湯|ゆ}: hot kudzu drink (sweetened thickened starch)
- {葛|くず}{餅|もち}: kudzu starch mochi (traditional sweet)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Kudzu is one of the {秋|あき}の{七草|ななくさ} (seven autumn flowers) celebrated in classical Japanese poetry. The starch made from its root has been valued in cuisine and traditional medicine for centuries.
